lines.trans: Poseidon is overwhelmingly ramping up its number of productions.

words.gram: て-form of auxiliary くる (go do something and return), used as a soft request.

lines.trans: Still, our studio competes through originality.
Long time no see! What are you all dressed up in an office suit for?
I just quit my company—all because of this!
An uncensored underground video of me.
Is it even possible to strip pixelation off a finished tape?
You can make it look faint, but removing it completely requires the original raw footage.
Wait—does that mean somebody stole our master footage?
Everyone harassed me at work, so I walked out and quit.
Who on earth did this!
Could the missing master tape really be...
I will never forgive whoever did this.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: 年内の制作本数を大幅に増やします。
examples.trans: We will sharply increase the number of productions before year's end.

examples.text: ポセイドン企画は圧倒的に制作本数を増やしてきてる。
examples.trans: Poseidon is overwhelmingly ramping up its number of productions.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 今店舗を増やして急成長してる店に掛け合ってみるんだ。
examples.trans: I will negotiate with a chain that is adding stores and growing fast right now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

examples.text: でもうちは個性で勝負だ、個性で。
examples.trans: Still, our studio competes through originality.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

meanings.en: a little while ago; just now
meanings.note: Refers to a recent point in time earlier the same day.

examples.text: さっきは何を売ったんだ？
examples.trans: What was it you sold earlier?

examples.text: さっき電話がありました。
examples.trans: There was a phone call just now.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Opposite of 表 (public surface); 裏の世界 means 'the underworld / hidden world'.

examples.text: 裏の世界を見せてやろうか。
examples.trans: Shall I show you the hidden world?
Write on the back of the paper.

meanings.note: Godan verb; コミュニケーションを取る means 'to communicate'.

examples.text: よく連絡を取っています。
メモを取ってもいいですか。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

examples.text: じゃあ誰かが素材を盗んだってことですか？
examples.trans: Wait—does that mean somebody stole our master footage?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Introduces a stunned guess ('don't tell me... / surely you aren't...').

examples.text: まさか来ないとは思いませんでした。
examples.trans: I never thought they wouldn't come.

examples.text: マスターテープがないんですよね。
現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Standard polite 'goodbye'.
